There is no evidence of obfuscated code, runtime exfiltration, or immediate execution of payloads during sourcing.

All content in the global scope aligns with standard AUR packaging practices. No malicious or suspicious execution occurs when this file is sourced for metadata extraction.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares standard fields such as package name, description, version, dependencies, source location, and checksums. The source is set to a Git repository over HTTPS from GitHub (https://github.com/rezigned/upmd.git), which aligns with the declared upstream URL. The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry is common for VCS (-git) packages in the AUR, as the content is inherently mutable and checksums cannot be pinned to a fixed release. This practice, while reducing reproducibility guarantees, is normal and expected for -git packages and does not constitute malicious behavior.

No executable code or scripts are present in this file. It contains only declarative packaging metadata. There are no network operations, file manipulations, or system commands that could pose a security risk. The dependencies listed (cargo, git, gcc-libs) are appropriate for building a Rust-based application from source. The package provides and conflicts with `upmd`, indicating it is an alternative build of the same project, which is typical for git versions of released software.

This file does not contain obfuscated content, unexpected downloads, or any mechanism for data exfiltration or remote code execution. All entries are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a Git-based package.
</details>
<evidence>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard AUR package for `upmd-git`, a tool that runs tasks and workflows from Markdown. It fetches the source from the declared upstream Git repository at https://github.com/rezigned/upmd.git, which matches the package's stated project URL. The `sha256sums` array uses "SKIP", which is expected and acceptable for VCS-based packages like `-git` packages, as the source is inherently mutable and checksums cannot be pinned.

The build process uses `cargo build --release` to compile the Rust-based project, which is appropriate given the makedepend `cargo`. The environment variables `CFLAGS`, `CXXFLAGS`, etc., are explicitly unset before building, which is a common practice to prevent unintended interference with Rust builds (Rust does not use these; Cargo ignores them, but this ensures cleanliness). The package installs only the compiled binary, license, and README into appropriate system directories.

No suspicious network operations, obfuscated code, unexpected file manipulations, or dangerous commands are present. All operations align with standard AUR packaging practices for a Git-based Rust application. The package does not introduce backdoors, execute untrusted code, or exfiltrate data.
</details>
